string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of the People\'s Republic of China and one of the country\'s four direct-administered municipalities. Located in northern China, it has been the political and cultural centre of the country for centuries and served as the imperial capital of the Ming and Qing dynasties. The city is home to the central government, Tiananmen Square, the Forbidden City and nearby sections of the Great Wall, and it is a major centre for education, research and international diplomacy. Beijing also became the first city to host both the Summer and the Winter Olympic Games.

Shanghai is a direct-administered municipality on China\'s eastern coast, at the mouth of the Yangtze River. It began as a modest fishing and trading settlement and grew rapidly after being opened to foreign trade in 1842, becoming the country\'s largest commercial port. Today Shanghai is a leading financial, shipping and manufacturing centre, known for the Pudong skyline, the Bund waterfront and one of the busiest container ports in the world. The city mixes historic lane houses with modern skyscrapers, hosts major cultural and sporting events, and ranks among the most populous cities in China.

Chongqing is a direct-administered municipality in south-west China, where the Jialing River meets the Yangtze. It became a municipality in 1997, making it one of the youngest, and by area one of the largest, in the country. Built across steep hills and river valleys, the city is famous for its dramatic night skyline, cable cars and spicy hotpot cuisine. Chongqing is a major industrial base for cars, motorcycles and electronics, and an important inland transport hub connected to the coast through the Yangtze. The municipality also includes large rural districts and part of the Three Gorges reservoir region.

Tianjin is a direct-administered municipality in northern China, on the coast of the Bohai Sea close to Beijing. It developed into a major port after being opened to foreign trade in 1860, and the old concession districts still contain European-style architecture. Today Tianjin is an important industrial and shipping centre, with a large automated port, a free-trade zone and growing aerospace and advanced manufacturing industries. High-speed rail links it with Beijing, forming a single metropolitan region. The city is also known for crosstalk comedy, its food streets and the Tianjin Eye ferris wheel on the Hai River.
